forecast_provider: Project model, not a NASA prediction
brief_favorable_conditions: Constant mist (humidity > 90 %), cool temperatures (14–19 °C), predictable seasonal rain and clean temporary pools.
why_these_variables: Mist/humidity, cool cloud-forest temperature and the dry-season rain that keeps breeding pools from drying out.
absolute_value_caution: Cloud-forest species: the NASA grid cell averages 381 m, far below the cloud forest (around 1,500 m), so absolute temperatures and humidity are several degrees warmer/drier than the habitat. Use the change versus normal, not the absolute value.

precip_dry_season.interval_note: Nominal 80% empirical residual band; not a calibrated guarantee. Validation windows overlap; limited residual sample.
precip_dry_season.data_caution: Reanalysis rainfall is the least reliable NASA POWER variable. Several sites show large multi-year shifts (e.g. Bramble Cay 2015–2025 about 42 % drier than 1981–2014; Monteverde dry-season rain about 3 times higher in 2009–2025 than in 1981–2008). A change-point test places these shifts in different years (1998–2015), so they do not point to a single data-source switch, but they may still be partly artificial. Rainfall forecasts that extend such shifts are uncertain: show the 80 % range and verify against local rain gauges before presenting them as fact.
precip_dry_season.summary_text: Dry-season rainfall in 2026–2030 is forecast to average 136.2 mm (nominal 80% band for 2030: 112.3–222.9 mm; coverage is not guaranteed), above the 1991–2020 average of 47.8 mm (+88.5 mm).
